newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch close to decision on airport privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Dutch close to decision on airport privatisation.

text.p: The Dutch government will decide in two to three weeks whether to sell off the bulk of its 76 percent stake in Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport, the transport ministry said on Thursday.
"The issue (of Schiphol's privatisation) is due to be settled in cabinet in two to three weeks," transport ministry spokesman Toon van Wijk told Reuters.
A government go-ahead for the sell-off would leave the Dutch state with a minority stake in the airport, the country's only international air hub.
Schiphol's other stakeholders are Amsterdam city council (22 percent) and Rotterdam city council (two percent).
Van Wijk said it had not yet been decided whether a possible privatisation would be effected through a bourse listing or a private share placement.

The government had been due to decide the sell-off by March 1, but the transport and finance ministries requested more time to assess the airport's pricing policy and the implications of its near-monopoly position.
"That study has now been completed," Van Wijk said, but declined to elaborate on the conclusions reached.
Dutch daily Algemeen Dagblad earlier reported transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma had approved the Schiphol privatisation and would recommend it to the cabinet after the Easter break.
But Van Wijk said he could not confirm the transport minister was recommending the deal.
